investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no node could accept the pod, so the agent VM was never provisioned. Because the VM was never created, the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod unscheduled for 144s, empty evidenceKeys — confirms the failure is not isolated to a single probe invocation.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod unscheduled for 146s, empty evidenceKeys — all three checks in the remote-agents feature share the same failure mode.

source-context.infra/evals/status/features.json:179-187: remote-agent-create is marked required=true with outageLatencyMs=360000; the observed latencyMs of 153010 is within the outage window, confirming the feature is in a degraded/outage state per its own registry thresholds.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector are occupied, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, making exhaustion more likely.
Tertiary — insufficient node pool scaling: the cluster may not have auto-scaled to add new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time, or the node pool ceiling has been reached.

Lower confidence — stale or leaked VM allocations: previously created remote agent VMs may not have been fully released, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a prior run leaked resources this could contribute.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable for ~144–147 seconds. The Kubernetes scheduler reported that 2 of 6 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero schedulable nodes and preventing any VM from being assigned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature (production-api environment) has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" confirms that no node could accept the pod, so the agent VM was never provisioned. Because the VM was never created, the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (line 256). This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: all available VM slots on the nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector are occupied, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector at all, meaning only 2 nodes are even eligible. If the affinity rules were recently tightened or node labels changed, the effective schedulable pool may have shrunk, making exhaustion more likely.
Tertiary — insufficient node pool scaling: the cluster may not have auto-scaled to add new kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in time, or the node pool ceiling has been reached.

Lower confidence — stale or leaked VM allocations: previously created remote agent VMs may not have been fully released, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new allocations. The withCleanup wrapper in the runner (run-status-probes.mjs line 1883) is intended to handle cleanup, but if a prior run leaked resources this could contribute.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-20 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has only 2 nodes capable of running kata peer-pod VMs, and both report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity. Because no pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure failure localized to the remote-agent VM scheduling layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving the remote-agent (kata peer-pod) workload in production-api has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector and are therefore ineligible. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every eval attempt to create a remote agent pod times out (~144–147 s) before the pod is ever placed, preventing any runtime evidence from being produced. The root cause is resource exhaustion of the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the eligible node pool, not an application-layer or eval-runner defect.
